entries.subject: Placement
entries.finding: Gaia DR3 source 1668690628102524672: position at J2016.0. Distance: Gaia DR3 parallax 29.0661 +/- 0.0217 mas (same row, RUWE 1.43): 34.40 pc, no zero-point correction; the RUWE is high, so the astrometry fits a single star poorly, and the parallax is used as published. Proper motion: Gaia DR3 (same row): -135.751, -37.089 mas/yr. Radial velocity from the same row.

entries.subject: Radius, mass and temperature
entries.finding: Radius 0.94 solar radii from Waite et al., arXiv:1611.07751, Table 1: radius 0.94 solar radii (https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07751). Mass 0.95 solar masses from Waite et al., arXiv:1611.07751, Table 1: mass 0.95 solar masses (https://arxiv.org/abs/1611.07751). Temperature 5647 K from TESS Input Catalog 8.2 (VizieR IV/39/tic82), TIC 159613900: Teff.

entries.subject: Color
entries.finding: A Planck spectrum at 5,647 K, because the Washington Double Star catalogue (Mason et al. 2001, AJ 122, 3466; VizieR B/wds/wds) lists WDS 14390+6417 KON 1: 0.8 arcsec apart, magnitudes 6 and 8.9: the companion gives 6.5% of the light, which a measured spectrum would blend with the star's. The color is the Planck spectrum at the star's temperature, through the CIE 1931 2-degree observer: #ffefe6. Routes tried in order: stis-ngsl: skipped; gaia-xp: skipped; pulkovo: skipped; kiehling: skipped; kharitonov: skipped; burnashev: skipped; planck: used.

entries.subject: Limb darkening
entries.finding: The disc is dimmed toward the limb by the quadratic law Claret & Bloemen (2011), A&A 529, A75 compute from ATLAS model atmospheres for the Johnson V band at 5,647 K and log g 4.47 (u1 0.488, u2 0.242): a model, because no fit of this star's limb is used.

entries.subject: Spin
entries.finding: Inclination 60 degrees from the line of sight, period 2.766 d, from Waite et al., arXiv:1611.07751, Table 1: rotation period 2.766 d and an axis 60 degrees from the line of sight, the values its magnetic maps were made with; the axis's direction on the sky is a convention.
